# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 101 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 51 | **Source Image:** source-texts/coptic/GTH_101_page_001.jpg

---

## Saying 101

**1** Jesus said: "Whoever does not hate his father and his mother in my way will not be able to be a disciple to me.

**2** And whoever does not love his father and his mother in my way will not be able to be a disciple to me.

**3** For my mother gave me death, but my true mother gave me life."

---

**Consensus Notes (SOPHIA):**

**Text:** Thomas's discipleship saying (cf. Luke 14:26) is remarkable for three reasons: (1) it adds a second clause requiring love *in my way* alongside the hate; (2) it introduces "my way" (*kata eme*) as the qualifier — both hate and love must be done as Jesus does them; (3) it concludes with the two-mothers saying: biological mother (death) vs. true mother (life).

**"My true mother"** — *tamaau nte tmhe*: literally "my mother of truth" — the divine mother, possibly the Holy Spirit (which in Syriac Christianity is feminine and maternal).

**"Gave me death"** — biological birth as the entry into mortality; "gave me life" — spiritual birth as the entry into true existence.

**"My way"** — PNEUMA's "earthly mother" is a clarifying addition not in the Coptic; SOPHIA preserves the unspecified "my mother" to let the mystery of the two-mothers stand.

**Synoptic Parallels:** Luke 14:26 ("If anyone comes to me and does not hate father and mother..."). Thomas adds the love clause and the two-mothers conclusion, neither of which has any Synoptic parallel.
